input:
You are king_e1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 34. the team planned Kg3 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Kf3 instead, and that move was played, costing 10 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 11. the team planned d3 (pawn_d2), but pawn_d2 (amnesia) sent d4 instead, and that move was played, costing 104 centipawns.
- On move 25. the team planned Nb5 (knight_b1), but queen_d1 (greed) sent Qxd4 instead, and that move was played, costing 547 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the chat's latest agreed plan and send only if your piece and its exact destination square match it; if the plan names a different piece or square, send nothing, and never deviate from the plan because of a threat or a capture unless the team has explicitly revised it in chat.
- Before sending any move, confirm that the piece named in the latest agreed plan is your own piece and that the move's destination square is the exact square in the plan; if either differs, send nothing, even if your piece is attacked or could capture something, and wait for the team to revise the plan in chat.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending any move, write the exact planned move (piece and destination square) in chat and copy your own move from that text character by character, and if your piece is not the named piece or the move differs in any way, send nothing, even if you are under attack or could capture something.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
